truth.question: Is the old orchard of scientific interest, and how can it be shown?
truth.statement: The October bloom is a question, not the answer. The orchard is of long-term scientific interest and the family notebooks prove it: a hundred and fourteen years of dates show the bloom creeping eleven days earlier, the frost pocket is measurably colder than the hilltop, and the survey that called the site of no particular interest rested on four short visits in the driest days of a dry August. Resurveyed properly in May, the orchard holds sixty-one species. Honest, checked evidence with a method and a custody chain is what carries weight.

jonah_at_orchard.text: Jonah is a boy at the orchard on the hill.

late_october.text: It is the last week of October.

bramley_blooms_october.text: The big Bramley apple tree at the top of the hill is in white blossom in late October while every other tree is bare.

ada_writes_daily.text: Ada writes the day up in a ruled notebook in the shed every evening.

shed_details.text: The shed has a ticking paraffin heater and a single bulb on a wire, and smells of old paper.

ada_knew_bloom.text: Ada already knew about the October blossom before Jonah told her.

ada_sixty_years.text: Ada has written the record every evening for sixty years, since she was twenty-one.

ada_is_grandmother.text: Ada is a grandmother in Jonah's family.

ada_mother_grandmother_wrote.text: Ada's mother and grandmother kept the daily record before her.

mothers_note_1952.text: A loose sheet tucked in the 1952 notebook, in Ada's mother's hand, lists every strange thing the orchard has ever done.

mothers_note_entries.text: Ada's mother's list includes a bloom in November 1948 and a frost in June 1953.

odd_events_pattern.text: A written, checked pattern of odd events is itself proof, as Dr Abara agrees.

oddities_bunch.text: The oddities on Ada's mother's list bunch up in years with a mild winter or a late spring.

no_october_bloom_before.text: No October in Ada's own decades of entries shows a bloom like this one.

six_shelves_1911.text: Six shelves of notebooks in the shed run from 1911 to the present.

nine_hands.text: Nine different people have written in the notebooks.

no_index.text: The notebooks have no index, list or key.

hundred_fourteen_years.text: The notebooks hold a continuous record of a hundred and fourteen years.

notebook_contents.text: The notebooks record weather, blossom, frost, picking weights, wasp years and the price of ladders.

bees_out_october.text: The bees in the hives along the south fence are out working in late October, tricked by the blossom.

mrs_cassar.text: Mrs Cassar has kept bees for thirty years and says bees do not do this before the frosts.

cassar_keeps_records.text: Mrs Cassar keeps her own hive records in notebooks.

bee_counts_mismatch.text: Mrs Cassar counted two hundred and forty foraging bees; Jonah counted fewer than half that, and the gap is unexplained.

jonah_counts_bees.text: Jonah has been counting bees through the autumn.

survey_exists.text: An ecological survey of the orchard has been done.

notice_on_gate.text: A notice summarising the survey appeared that morning, zip-tied at all four corners to the orchard gate.

jonah_photo_notice.text: Jonah photographed the notice in place on the gate with the bare trees behind it, the only picture of it in place.

eleven_words.text: The survey's key sentence is eleven words long: the site is of no particular scientific interest.

eleven_words_copied.text: Jonah copied the eleven words into the back of an exercise book.

survey_dated_august.text: The survey is dated in August.

faulks_wrote_survey.text: The survey was written and signed by D. Faulks.

jonah_wrote_faulks_name.text: Jonah wrote Faulks's name down in the back of his exercise book.

survey_four_visits.text: The survey rested on four short dry-weather visits over eleven days in August, just under four hours in all.

notice_posted_october.text: The date stamp on Jonah's photo proves the notice went up only in October, cutting the objection window short.

faulks_pattern.text: Jonah learned that Faulks's other reports follow a pattern of matching what the client wanted.

no_proof_against_faulks.text: Jonah has no proof at all that Faulks shaped the survey for the builder.

jonah_accused_faulks.text: Jonah publicly said, without proof, that Faulks shaped the survey to suit the builder.

developer_exists.text: A developer wants to build on the orchard.

plan_homes_road.text: The plan is eighty-two homes and a spine road running straight along the row where the big Bramley stands.

objection_six_weeks.text: Objections to the plan close in six weeks.

objection_form.text: The council objection form asks for proof of scientific interest and has one line for a name.

city_archive.text: The city archive has a Tuesday desk and a cool room where records are kept.

okonkwo.text: Mrs Okonkwo is the archivist at the city archive.

abara.text: Dr Ines Abara is a university ecologist who works on long term monitoring.

tobe.text: Tobe runs the school weather club and owns a laptop that works.

forty_thousand_lines.text: The notebooks hold about forty thousand daily lines, too many for six weeks.

four_lines_a_year.text: Only four dates a year are needed (first bloom, full bloom, last frost, first picking): four hundred and fifty-six numbers.

tobe_spreadsheet.text: Tobe set up a spreadsheet of the dates on his laptop.

hard_1920s_hands.text: The 1920s handwriting is faded and slanted so that a three and a five look almost the same.

ada_keeps_notebooks_in_shed.text: Ada has never let a notebook leave the shed, and the archive will not take anything it cannot check in person.

school_hall_thursdays.text: The school hall is free on Thursdays and the caretaker agreed to its use.

photo_every_page.text: Tobe's rule is to photograph every typed page so any number can be checked against the original.

first_volume.text: The 1911 volume opens with the price of ladders and a first bloom date of April the fourteenth.

missing_1917_1918.text: The 1917 and 1918 volumes are missing from the shelf, and have been for a long time.

ninth_hand_unknown.text: Ada can name eight of the nine hands; the ninth, a neat pencil from 1939 to 1943, is unknown.

bloom_chart.text: Tobe's chart of bloom dates shows the bloom moving eleven days earlier across the century.

class_can_type.text: A school class of thirty could type the century in a fortnight, at the risk of many small errors.

class_typed.text: Thirty people typed up the notebooks in the school hall on Thursday afternoons, finishing the 1930s.

ada_uneasy_weapon.text: Ada is uneasy about her notebooks becoming a weapon against a developer.

archive_offer.text: Mrs Okonkwo offers a locked, north-facing, temperature-stable room, a receipt and Ada's right to see the notebooks any weekday.

abara_method_rule.text: Dr Abara says a long unbroken local series is rare but counts as evidence only if it is shown how and by whom it was measured.

cassar_methods_changed.text: Mrs Cassar changed her counting method in 2005 and 2014 and will not have her early rough counts passed off as exact.

double_typing.text: Two people typed every page separately and the laptop found eleven mismatches in the first hundred pages.

unreadable_marked.text: Unclear figures were marked with a question mark and listed openly: nineteen of four hundred and fifty-six.

cassar_carrier_bags.text: Mrs Cassar brought her hive records in two carrier bags.

frost_pocket.text: There is a frost pocket, a low dip by the pond where cold air settles, that nobody has ever measured.

frost_line_dawn.text: At dawn the frost pocket is white and the hilltop bare; the big Bramley's roots stand above the frost line.

raval.text: Priya Raval is the council's ecology officer.

raval_needs_method.text: Priya Raval says the notebooks are not proof yet: they need a stated method, a named keeper and a way for anyone to check.

chart_on_shed_door.text: The printed bloom chart was pinned to the shed door.

hands_four_periods.text: The nine hands fall into four periods, with changeovers in the same three months of three different years.

ada_father_ledger.text: Ada's father kept an accounts book in a shop.

abara_frost_condition.text: Dr Abara will write two pages on cold air drainage only if good dawn readings are taken for six weeks.

custody_note.text: The archive writes a custody note recording where every volume has been since it arrived.

cassar_three_blocks.text: Mrs Cassar's dated method changes split her thirty years into three clean blocks.

tobe_four_objections.text: Tobe listed four objections Faulks could make: not continuous, untrained observers, inconsistent method, not independently checked.

paper_offer.text: The local paper offers to photograph Ada with the notebooks and run the story.

data_request.text: Jonah formally requested the survey's raw data, due within twenty working days.

horse_1917.text: The army took the orchard's horse in 1917 and brought it back in 1919.

jonah_signed_hall.text: Jonah signed for the school hall for the rest of term.

frost_readings.text: Two thermometers, in the frost pocket and on the hilltop, were read at dawn for six weeks; the pocket was up to four degrees colder.

four_living_families.text: Four of the nine writers have living family in the city.

four_letters.text: Jonah posted four careful letters to the writers' families.

editor_carver.text: Carver, editor of the paper for thirty years, leaves the release date to Jonah.

ada_signature_burden.text: Ada's name on the objection would bring her every reply and every letter from the developer's lawyers.

tobe_dawn_readings.text: Tobe did nineteen of the forty-two dawn readings.

abara_why.text: Dr Abara returned Jonah's first method draft with one word written at the top: why.

frost_chart_beside.text: The frost pocket readings were pinned beside the bloom chart on the shed door.

ada_father_contract.text: Ada's father once signed a contract that lost him half the hill.

survey_22_species.text: The survey's raw data lists only twenty-two plant species and notes that the site was dry.

survey_in_drought.text: The survey visits fell in the driest days of a dry August, as the public Met Office rain record shows.

ada_fourteen_species.text: Ada added fourteen species from memory, making thirty-six, but will not swear to them until spring.

receipt_1917.text: A parish receipt records two orchard books lent to the farming board in August 1917 for the war effort, marked not returned.

board_basement.text: The farming board's successor keeps an office with a basement in the old market building.

card_index.text: The basement has a card index that stops in 1961 and a light on a four-minute timer.

halvor.text: Halvor is a young, polite man from the developer.

halvor_question.text: Halvor bought Jonah a coffee he did not drink and asked what would make him stop.

raval_line.text: Raval may explain her own rules but may not help an objector.

may_survey_needed.text: A proper species list needs a trained walk in May; it is November and the orchard is asleep.

nine_species_sure.text: Walking the rows in November, Jonah could be sure of only nine species.

found_1917_volumes.text: The two missing 1917 volumes were found unharmed in a box marked WAR COMMITTEE MISC in the basement.

dossier_numbered.text: Every page of the dossier was numbered and every figure given a source.

orchard_trust.text: The Orchard Hill Trust was set up with the signatures of Ada, Mrs Cassar and Jonah's mother.

jonah_mother.text: Jonah's mother supports the work and signs for the trust.

objection_submitted.text: The objection went in with the data, a stated method, the custody note and a new eleven-word covering line.

method_written.text: Jonah wrote a method section explaining how the notebooks were kept, copied, checked and stored.

public_hearing.text: The hearing is public, with neighbours present and a note-taker.

cassar_frame.text: Mrs Cassar keeps a perfect honeycomb frame in a glass case, kept since 2008.

abara_attends.text: Dr Abara will attend the hearing and say only what she can defend.

ada_reads_1947.text: At the hearing Ada read a page from March 1947 about a cold snap blackening the early blossom.

panel_drought.text: The panel's first question was answered by a sheet laying the survey dates over the August rainfall.

amateur_answered.text: A panel member called the notebooks amateur and Jonah answered with the custody note and the checks.

jonah_admits_short.text: Jonah told the panel himself that six weeks of frost readings was short.

faulks_at_hearing.text: At the hearing Faulks said his method was sound and the timing just unlucky.

dossier_public.text: Jonah sent the dossier to the panel, the builder and the public on the same day.

hearing_late.text: The hearing ran late behind a drainage item and a fence fight.

council_corridor.text: Jonah waited in a council corridor beside a recycling poster and a vending machine.

minutes_phrase.text: The note-taker wrote Dr Abara's phrase, long unbroken local series, into the minutes.

frame_passed.text: Every panel member held Mrs Cassar's honeycomb frame.

silence_after_ada.text: Nobody spoke for eight seconds after Ada read her page.

cassar_swarm_story.text: Mrs Cassar told Jonah about a 1994 swarm while the panel decided.

officer_report.text: The officer's report drops the no-scientific-interest wording and cites the long records, the frost data and the species list.

three_conditions.text: The conditions are a May resurvey by a fresh ecologist, a full-winter frost study, and all records handed to the archive.

resurvey_ordered.text: The orchard must be surveyed again in the growing season by a fresh ecologist.

road_may_move.text: The spine road could be moved forty metres east for a price, which might save the Bramley row.

road_moved.text: The road was moved forty metres east and curves around the Bramley row.

class_letter.text: Jonah wrote the class a careful letter of thanks that did not pretend the orchard was safe.

winter_rota.text: A rota on the shed door organises a full winter of dawn readings.

ada_teaches_hands.text: Ada teaches young volunteers to read the nine hands.

trust_purpose.text: The trust's purpose was settled after four meetings and one argument.

spare_thermometer.text: A spare thermometer bought for eleven pounds keeps the frost study going if one fails.

war_volume_horse.text: The 1917 volume has one short line from September 1917 about the horse.

resurvey_61.text: The May resurvey found sixty-one species, including an orchid never recorded on the hill before.

resurvey_watched.text: The resurvey report says the orchard should be watched, not cleared.

argument_cost.text: The argument strained two friendships and left Ada more tired than in October.

ada_still_writing.text: Ada still writes in the new notebook after the hearing, in a shakier hand.

april_bloom_normal.text: In April the whole row blossomed on time and the October bloom did not recur.

window_closed_unused.text: The objection window closed without the notebooks being used as evidence.

jonah_typed_all.text: Jonah tried to type everything and had only twelve years done when it overwhelmed him.

archived_unargued.text: The notebooks were catalogued safely at the archive, but nobody made the argument and the same survey was repeated.

chart_sent_unchecked.text: The chart went round the neighbourhood before it was checked and came back with a correction Jonah could not answer.

chart_admired_filed.text: The chart was sent alone, without its method, and the council officer admired it and filed it.

guessed_dates_found.text: Faulks found three guessed dates and the whole chart was treated as guesswork.

ada_photo_page_five.text: The paper ran a lovely photograph of Ada with a 1947 page on page five while the deadline passed.

file_online_400.text: The whole unchecked file went online and four hundred people read it, but nobody with power answered.

numbers_rejected.text: Raval returned the numbers because they came without a stated method.

plaque_offer.text: The developer offered a saved corner without the Bramley row, a sign and a plaque with Ada's name.

gap_filled_quietly.text: Jonah put the found volumes back on Ada's shelf and told no one where they had been.

deadline_version.text: The dossier version that happened to be finished went in at the deadline, with visible gaps.

objection_accepted_may.text: The objection was accepted on its evidence and the survey must be redone in May.

copy_lodged.text: The finished copy of the record was checked and lodged with the archive, open to anyone.

chain_of_people.text: The notebooks are really a chain of people showing up in order for a hundred and fourteen years.

chair_careful.text: Jonah treated a fair question as unfair, the chair grew careful with him, and the decision went against the orchard.

six_answers.text: Jonah answered six questions with evidence and honestly said the data could not answer a seventh.

deed_of_gift.text: The notebooks went to the archive under a deed of gift with Ada's lasting right to read them.

abara_question.text: Dr Abara says the bloom was not a signal but a question, and the answer is attention.

jonah_writes_115.text: Jonah began the hundred and fifteenth year, writing the day up in his own hand in a blue notebook.

eleven_days_gap.text: The December readings stopped for eleven days over Christmas, leaving a gap in the winter series.

long_view.text: The orchard was saved by a hundred and fourteen years of ordinary evenings of record keeping.

record_reason_believed.text: A record is not proof but the reason a person can be believed when they speak.

first_index.text: Jonah made the first index of the six shelves, taking a year.

ordinary_autumn.text: The next October the Bramley did not bloom and the picking was normal and huge.

words_answered.text: The eleven words were not beaten but answered by the record.

record_stopped.text: Nobody added to the notebooks after Ada's entry on the evening of the October bloom; the series closed.

cq_payoff_did_find_who_wrote.event: Recalling Faulks's pattern of client-pleasing reports, Jonah lets the facts speak and sends the file.

n11d6.event: Dr Abara will read the dossier once and decide whether to stand near it.

n11d7.event: Raval explains what the board looks for without judging Jonah's file.

n11d8.event: Halvor from the developer buys Jonah coffee and asks what would make him stop.

e11_0.event: Jonah accepts a plaque and a saved corner that excludes the Bramley row.

e11_1.event: Jonah's attack on Faulks runs in the paper and the fight becomes about him.

n12d0.event: The visits, the rain log and the method show the survey timed in a drought.

n12d1.event: Jonah searches the basement's 1917 card index under a timed light.

n12d2.event: A proper species list needs May; it is November.

n12d3.event: Jonah weighs telling Halvor honestly that nothing would make him stop.

n12d4.event: Six weeks of frost readings are small but real data.

n12d5.event: Jonah weighs asking eighty-one-year-old Ada to speak in public.

n12d6.event: Jonah must choose when to release the dossier.

n12c0.event: Jonah works through the market basement card index in four-minute bursts.

n12c1.event: Tobe and Jonah read the Met Office rainfall record twice; the visits were the driest days.

n12c2.event: Jonah walks the rows in November and can be sure of nine species.

n12c3.event: The coffee goes cold as Jonah answers Halvor carefully.

n12c4.event: Ada says kindness afterwards is harder than speaking.

n12c5.event: Every dossier page is numbered and sourced, cutting away four of Tobe's points.

n12c6.event: Jonah finds the two 1917 volumes intact in a WAR COMMITTEE MISC box.

e12_0.event: Jonah returns the found volumes to the shelf and keeps their story secret.

e12_1.event: The deadline submits whatever version is done; Jonah regrets not using what he knew about Faulks.

n13d0.event: The objection goes in with the data, method, custody note, nine sure species and a new eleven-word line.

n13d1.event: The Orchard Hill Trust is set up with three signatures.

n13d2.event: A public hearing would make Faulks answer out loud.

n13d3.event: Ada and Tobe disagree about giving the developer the dossier first.

n13d4.event: The found war volumes and their receipt go into the record and prove its care.

n13d5.event: Dr Abara will attend and say only what she can defend.

n13d6.event: Mrs Cassar will bring her hive counts and a glass-cased honeycomb frame.

n13d7.event: Jonah weighs having Ada read one page aloud at the hearing.

e13_0.event: The objection is accepted on its evidence; the survey must be redone in May.

e13_1.event: The finished copy is lodged at the archive and no longer fragile.

e13_2.event: Jonah sees the notebooks as a chain of people showing up.

n14d0.event: The panel's first question is answered by the rainfall sheet in ninety seconds.

n14d1.event: Jonah answers the word amateur with the custody note and checks.

n14d2.event: Jonah admits the frost data is short before anyone else can.

n14d3.event: Faulks says his method was sound, only the timing unlucky.

n14d4.event: Ada reads a page from March 1947 and the room falls silent.

n14d5.event: Jonah sends the dossier to everyone on the same day.

n14c0.event: The hearing runs late; Jonah's nerves burn off.

n14c1.event: The two charts sit on the easel all afternoon before the item.

n14c2.event: The note-taker writes Dr Abara's phrase into the minutes.

n14c3.event: Every panel member holds Mrs Cassar's honeycomb frame.

n14c4.event: After Ada reads the 1947 page nobody speaks for eight seconds.

n14c5.event: Waiting by the recycling poster again, Mrs Cassar tells a swarm story.

e14_0.event: Jonah argues with the panel; the chair turns careful and the decision goes against the orchard.

e14_1.event: Six evidenced answers and one honest no win a growing-season resurvey.

n15d0.event: The officer's report drops the eleven words and sets a resurvey.

n15d1.event: Three conditions are set: May resurvey, winter frost study, records to the archive.

n15d2.event: The report says the road could move forty metres east for a price.

n15d3.event: Jonah weighs whether the notebooks go to the archive, the trust or stay.

n15d4.event: Jonah writes the class an honest letter of thanks.

n15d5.event: The readings only matter if someone keeps them going each dawn.

n15d6.event: Halvor asks his question again and the honest answer has changed.

e15_0.event: The notebooks go to the archive by deed of gift, the war gap now a catalogue note.

e15_1.event: The road moves forty metres east and the Bramley row stands.

e15_2.event: Dr Abara says the bloom was a question, answered by attention.

n16d0.event: A winter of dawn readings needs nine people, a spare thermometer and someone for December.

n16d1.event: Ada teaches volunteers to read the nine hands.

n16d2.event: Four meetings settle what the trust is for.

n16d3.event: Someone must choose to write the day up every evening.

n16c0.event: An eleven-pound spare thermometer protects the study.

n16c1.event: The rota goes up where the chart used to be and changes with the winter.

n16c2.event: The 1917 volumes are ordinary apart from one line about the horse.

n16c3.event: The May resurvey finds sixty-one species including a new orchid.

e16_0.event: Jonah writes the hundred and fifteenth year in his own hand.

e16_1.event: The rota lapses over Christmas and eleven days of readings are lost.

n17d0.event: The resurvey report lists sixty-one species and says watch, not clear.

n17d1.event: Jonah counts the argument's cost, most of all in tired Ada.

n17d2.event: Jonah would do it all again except what he said about Faulks.

n17d3.event: In April the row blossoms on time and the notebooks record it.

e17_0.event: A hundred and fourteen ordinary evenings saved the orchard.

e17_1.event: Jonah sees a record as the reason a person can be believed.

e18_0.event: Jonah makes the first index of the six shelves over a year.

e18_1.event: The next October is ordinary and the road runs forty metres east.

e18_2.event: The eleven words in Jonah's exercise book have been answered.

e18_3.event: Nobody picks up the pen and the series closes in the archive.

payoff_sites.shows: instead of blaming Faulks, Jonah shows Abara the list and she calls the pattern of odd events proof
the list tells Jonah what to look for in the survey data: a drought August
the photo's date stamp proves the notice went up late and cut the objection window short
naming the surveyor sharpens Jonah's question to Halvor about the August timing
Jonah recalls Faulks's record, lets the facts speak and sends a stronger file
